• A folder's size is the sum of its children, computed in post-order: size(node) = sum of file sizes + folders.map(size). Cache the results in a Map so toggling the sort doesn't recompute anything.
  • For the scan animation, flatten the post-order sequence into a list, then reveal each folder's total on a setTimeout/setInterval tick (or with rAF).

todo-app.desc: The "Hello World" of machine coding, where nailing the edge cases sets you apart.
todo-app.q: How will you solve this problem? Todo App with Filters

accordion.q: How will you solve this problem? Accordion Component
accordion.why:
• Single mode: store one openId. Multiple mode: store a Set of openIds. Render each item as open or closed based on whether its id is in the open set.
  • For a smooth height animation, transition max-height from 0 to max-content, or use a ref to measure the content height and animate to that value.

modal.desc: Looks simple, but the gotchas (focus trap, scroll lock, portal) reveal your seniority.
modal.q: How will you solve this problem? Modal / Dialog Component
modal.what:
Build a reusable Modal component. It should render in a portal, trap focus inside, close on backdrop click and the ESC key, lock body scroll while open, and support a header/body/footer layout.

Requirements

  • Render into document.body via createPortal
  • Close on backdrop click (not on clicks inside the modal)
  • Close on ESC keydown
  • Lock body scroll (overflow: hidden) while open
  • Focus trap: Tab cycles only within the modal
  • The first focusable element receives focus on open
  • Restore focus to the trigger element on close

Concepts: useEffect · createPortal · refs · keyboard events · focus management
modal.why:
• Use useRef to store the element that had focus before the modal opened. On close, call storedRef.current.focus().
  • Focus trap: on a Tab keydown, check whether the focused element is the last focusable one; if so, move focus to the first. Query all focusable elements inside the modal to find them.

star-rating.q: How will you solve this problem? Star Rating Component
star-rating.what:
Build a StarRating component with a controlled rating, hover preview, half-star support, a readonly mode, and custom size and color. Fire an onChange(rating) callback.

Requirements

  • Render N stars (default 5, configurable)
  • Hovering a star previews that rating
  • Clicking sets the rating (fires onChange)
  • Readonly mode: no interaction
  • Half stars: hovering the left half of a star gives an x.5 rating
  • ARIA: role="radiogroup" on the container, role="radio" with aria-checked on each star

Concepts: useState · mouse events · controlled components · ARIA · CSS

tabs.q: How will you solve this problem? Tabs Component
tabs.what:
Build a Tabs component that accepts [{id, label, content}]. Support keyboard navigation (arrow keys), lazy-loaded panels, controlled and uncontrolled modes, and horizontal and vertical orientation.

Requirements

  • Clicking a tab shows its panel
  • Arrow Left/Right (horizontal) or Up/Down (vertical) moves between tabs
  • Home/End jump to the first/last tab
  • Lazy: render a panel's content only once its tab has been active (mount once, keep it in the DOM)
  • ARIA: role="tablist", role="tab", role="tabpanel" and aria-selected

Concepts: useState · keyboard events · ARIA · lazy rendering · controlled components
tabs.why:
• For lazy rendering, track a Set of "everActivated" tab ids and render a panel only if its id is in the set. Hide inactive panels with CSS (hidden) instead of unmounting them.
  • For keyboard support, keep refs to all the tab elements. On an arrow key, focus the adjacent tab with tabRef[newIndex].focus().

countdown.q: How will you solve this problem? Countdown Timer
countdown.why:
• Use setInterval inside useEffect, and clear it on pause and on unmount. Keep the remaining time in state; on each tick, decrement it and check for zero.
  • For the SVG ring: circumference = 2*π*r and stroke-dashoffset = circumference * (1 - progress). Animate it with a CSS transition.

pagination.q: How will you solve this problem? Pagination Component

otp-input.q: How will you solve this problem? OTP Input Component

searchable-dropdown.q: How will you solve this problem? Searchable Dropdown
searchable-dropdown.why:
• Put a ref on the container div to detect outside clicks. In useEffect, call document.addEventListener("mousedown", handler), and check ref.current.contains(event.target).
  • For text highlighting, split each option label by the search term and wrap the matching parts in .

progress-bar.desc: Clamping, threshold colors and indeterminate mode: the small details interviewers check.
progress-bar.q: How will you solve this problem? Progress Bar Component
progress-bar.what:
Build a ProgressBar component with the props value, max (default 100) and color. Clamp the value to [0, max]. Support threshold-based color zones and an indeterminate animation mode.

Requirements

  • value is clamped between 0 and max (no negative or overflowing width)
  • Width is computed as value / max * 100%
  • Threshold zones via a config prop (danger/warning/success colors)
  • Indeterminate mode: continuous animation, no value shown
  • Accessible: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max
  • Optional text label on the left and percentage on the right

Concepts: CSS width transition · Math.min/Math.max clamping · conditional styling · ARIA

theme-toggle.desc: A staple product question: CSS variables, persistence and system preference.
theme-toggle.q: How will you solve this problem? Theme Toggle (Dark/Light)
theme-toggle.what:
Build a ThemeToggle that switches between light and dark themes. Persist the choice in localStorage, and on the first visit respect prefers-color-scheme. Apply the theme through a data-theme attribute on the root element and CSS custom properties.

Requirements

  • The toggle button switches themes with a smooth transition
  • The choice is persisted to localStorage and restored on reload
  • The first visit uses the prefers-color-scheme media query
  • Theme applied via a data-theme="dark" attribute plus CSS variables
  • No flash of the wrong theme on load (early inline init)
  • aria-pressed reflects the current theme for screen readers

Concepts: CSS variables · localStorage · prefers-color-scheme · useEffect
theme-toggle.why:
• Define the CSS variables on :root for light and on [data-theme="dark"] for dark. The theme state is localStorage.theme ?? the system preference.
  • To avoid a flash, set document.documentElement.dataset.theme in a tiny inline script before the app hydrates.

traffic-light.q: How will you solve this problem? Traffic Light
traffic-light.what:
Build a TrafficLight component that automatically cycles Red (3s) -> Green (3s) -> Yellow (1s). A control panel lets you pause and resume and switch colors manually (manual mode cancels the auto-cycle until it is resumed).

Requirements

  • Auto cycle: Red 3s -> Green 3s -> Yellow 1s, repeating
  • Only one bulb is lit at a time
  • Pause/Resume buttons freeze and continue the cycle
  • Manual color buttons switch immediately and pause the cycle
  • Resume restarts the auto-cycle from the current color
  • Durations are configurable via a prop
  • Accessible: role="status" announces the current color

Concepts: useEffect · state machine · setTimeout vs setInterval · cleanup
traffic-light.why:
• Model the state as {color, manual}. One useEffect keyed on color schedules the next transition with setTimeout(duration); clear it on pause and on unmount.
  • Manual click: call setColor and setManual(true). Resume: call setManual(false) so the effect re-runs and continues the cycle.

grid-light.desc: The Flipkart machine coding round: click a cell, then watch the chain reaction.
grid-light.q: How will you solve this problem? Grid Light (Flipkart)
grid-light.what:
Build a GridLight game. Render a 3x3 (configurable N x M) grid of cells. Clicking a cell lights it up. When ALL cells are lit, turn them off one by one in reverse click order, 500ms apart.

Requirements

  • Configurable grid size (rows, cols)
  • Clicking turns a cell on (one-way: off -> on)
  • Track the order in which cells were lit
  • When all cells are lit, turn them off in reverse click order, 500ms apart
  • Input is locked during the reset animation
  • A restart/new-game button clears all state
  • Cells are square buttons with clear lit and unlit visuals

Concepts: useState · setTimeout chain · queue ordering · disabling input during animation

navbar.q: How will you solve this problem? Responsive Navbar with Mobile Menu
navbar.what:
Build a Navbar component. Desktop: horizontal links. Mobile (below 768px): a hamburger icon toggles a dropdown menu. Highlight the active link with scroll-spy. Support closing on outside click and ESC, smooth scrolling, and a sticky navbar that gains a shadow after scrolling.

Requirements

  • Desktop layout: logo plus horizontal nav links
  • Mobile: the hamburger button opens and closes the menu
  • The menu closes on link click, outside click and ESC
  • Active link highlighted via IntersectionObserver scroll-spy
  • Sticky navbar with a shadow only after 10px of scroll
  • Accessible: aria-expanded on the hamburger, aria-label on the nav
  • Smooth scrolling to anchors

Concepts: useState · useEffect · useRef · media queries · IntersectionObserver · outside click
navbar.why:
• Track the open state, plus a ref on the nav wrapper for outside-click detection (a document mousedown listener with a contains check).
  • Scroll-spy: observe the sections and set activeId to the section closest to the top of the viewport.

stepper.desc: The progress tracker MakeMyTrip asked in their SSE round: dynamic step count, one active step.
stepper.q: How would you solve this problem? Stepper / Steps Indicator
stepper.what:
Build a Stepper component that renders a horizontal step indicator: completed steps (with a check), the active step (highlighted), and upcoming steps, joined by connectors. Support a dynamic step count, click-to-navigate, a vertical variant, and onChange(stepIndex).

Requirements

  • Render N steps with connectors between them
  • Per-step states: completed (check), active (current), upcoming
  • Steps configurable via [{label, status?}] or controlled through a current prop
  • Clicking a step navigates to it (fires onChange)
  • Adding or removing steps re-renders correctly
  • Vertical orientation variant
  • Accessible: aria-current="step" on the active step

Concepts: array rendering · controlled vs uncontrolled · conditional styling · ARIA

autocomplete.desc: The canonical React machine coding problem: debounce, API calls, keyboard navigation, highlighting.
autocomplete.q: How would you solve this problem? Autocomplete with Debounce + Highlight
autocomplete.what:
Build a production-quality Autocomplete component. Debounce the API call (300ms), support keyboard navigation of the results (Up/Down/Enter/Escape), highlight the matched text, show loading and error states, and cache results to avoid duplicate requests.

Requirements

  • Debounce the API call by 300ms
  • Show a loading spinner during the fetch
  • Keyboard navigation: Up/Down move the selection, Enter picks it, Escape closes
  • Highlight the matching substring in each result
  • Cache results by query string (avoid duplicate API calls)
  • Handle API errors gracefully, with a retry option
  • Clear-input button

Concepts: useCallback · useRef · debounce · useReducer for complex state · caching
autocomplete.why:
• Keep the debounce timer in a useRef (not state) to avoid re-renders. Cache with a useRef Map: queryCache.current.get(query).
  • Manage state with useReducer: {results, loading, error, selectedIndex, isOpen}. Each action updates only its own slice.

infinite-scroll.desc: IntersectionObserver, pagination and race conditions: all the real-world complexity.
infinite-scroll.q: How will you solve this problem? Infinite Scroll List
infinite-scroll.what:
Build an InfiniteScrollList component that fetches paginated data and shows a loading indicator at the bottom. When the indicator becomes visible, load the next page. Handle the loading state, error state, end-of-data state, and duplicate-fetch prevention.

Requirements

  • Use IntersectionObserver on a sentinel element at the bottom
  • Fetch the next page when the sentinel enters the viewport
  • Show a skeleton or spinner while the next page loads
  • Show "All items loaded" when the data is exhausted
  • Prevent duplicate requests (lock during an in-flight fetch)
  • Error boundary plus a retry button on fetch failure

Concepts: useEffect · useRef · IntersectionObserver · async state · pagination
infinite-scroll.why:
• Attach a ref to a
    at the bottom of the list and observe it in useEffect. When it intersects, nothing is loading, and hasMore is true, call fetchNextPage().
  • Prevent duplicates with a loading ref (not state) checked inside the observer callback, because state read inside a closure can be stale.

multistep-form.desc: The most common enterprise machine coding problem: form state, validation and navigation.
multistep-form.q: How will you solve this problem? Multi-step Form with Validation

data-table.q: How will you solve this problem? Sortable + Filterable Data Table
data-table.why:
• Derive sortedData and filteredData from the raw data with useMemo, and never mutate the original.
  • Sort state: {column: null, direction: "asc"}. On click, toggle the direction if it's the same column; otherwise set the new column with "asc".

toast.q: How will you solve this problem? Toast Notification System
toast.why:
• Store the toasts in a Context that provides addToast/removeToast. Each toast has an id (Date.now()), type, message and duration.
  • To pause on hover: on mouseenter, clear the auto-dismiss timer and store the remaining time. On mouseleave, start a new timer with the remaining time.

kanban.desc: The hardest of the beginner-level React problems: drag & drop plus state management is the gauntlet.
kanban.q: How will you solve this problem? Kanban Board with Drag & Drop

shopping-cart.q: How will you solve this problem? Shopping Cart

file-upload.q: How will you solve this problem? File Upload with Preview & Progress

image-carousel.q: How will you solve this problem? Image Carousel / Slider
image-carousel.what:
Build an ImageCarousel component with an images[] prop and an optional autoPlayInterval. Features: next/prev arrows, dot indicators, clickable thumbnails, infinite wrap-around, auto-play that pauses on hover, and smooth slide transitions. Handle the 1-image and 0-image edge cases.

Requirements

  • Next/Prev buttons cycle through images and wrap around infinitely
  • Dot indicators show the active image and jump to any image
  • Auto-play every N seconds; pauses on hover and after manual interaction
  • Smooth slide/translate transition between images
  • Thumbnail strip (configurable)
  • Edge cases: 1 image hides the arrows, 0 images shows an empty state
  • Adjacent images are preloaded for fast navigation

Concepts: useState · useRef · setInterval · CSS transform · index modulo

chip-input.desc: Invite chips, tag inputs, email chips: the same problem shows up at every product company.
chip-input.q: How would you solve this problem? Chips / Tags Input
chip-input.what:
Build a ChipsInput component. The user types a value and presses Enter or comma to add a chip. Backspace on an empty input removes the last chip, and Backspace on a focused chip removes that chip. Support duplicate prevention, a max chip count, a validation callback, and a suggestions dropdown. Call onChange(values) whenever the chips change.

Requirements

  • Enter or comma adds the typed text as a chip
  • Backspace on an empty input removes the last chip
  • Backspace on a focused chip removes that chip
  • Duplicates and invalid values are rejected via a validation callback
  • Optional max chips limit
  • Suggestions dropdown filtered by the input; arrow keys + Enter to pick
  • Chips can be removed with their x button
  • Controlled: onChange(values) reflects the chips array

Concepts: controlled inputs · keyboard events · array state · focus management
chip-input.why:
• Keep the values as string[] state. In onKeyDown, Enter or comma validates the text, adds it, and clears the input; Backspace on an empty input pops the last chip.
  • Give each chip a tabIndex. In the Backspace handler, check document.activeElement === chip to remove a focused chip.

transfer-list.q: How would you solve this problem? Transfer List
transfer-list.what:
Build a TransferList component with two panes: Available (left) and Selected (right). The user checks items and moves them with bulk action buttons. Disable an action when nothing is checked in its source pane. Support select-all per pane, independent search, move-all, and item counts.

Requirements

  • A checkbox per item in both panes
  • Bulk buttons: Move to selected -> and <- Move to available
  • Each bulk button is disabled when its source pane has no checked items
  • Select-all checkbox per pane (indeterminate when only some are checked)
  • A search box filters each pane independently
  • Move-all quick actions
  • Item counts per pane (3 of 10 selected)

Concepts: Set state · bulk actions · indeterminate checkbox · filtering
transfer-list.why:
• Keep available[], selected[], and two checked Sets. A transfer removes the checked items from the source list, adds them to the target, and clears the source's checked set.
  • Select-all is checked when checked.size === list.length. It is indeterminate when checked.size > 0 and < list.length; set the DOM indeterminate property via a ref.

checkbox-tree.q: How would you solve this problem? Nested Checkbox Tree
checkbox-tree.what:
Build a CheckboxTree from nested data: [{id, label, children?}]. Each parent checkbox is checked (all children checked), unchecked (none), or indeterminate (some). Checking a parent toggles all its descendants, and checking a child recomputes its ancestors. Support expand/collapse, defaultExpanded, and a search that auto-expands matching branches.

Requirements

  • Recursive tree rendering with per-node expand/collapse
  • Parent state is derived from its children: checked / unchecked / indeterminate
  • Toggling a parent toggles all its descendants
  • Toggling a leaf recomputes the state of every ancestor
  • Expand-all / collapse-all buttons
  • Search highlights matches and auto-expands their branches
  • onChange(checkedIds) emits the flat set of checked ids

Concepts: recursive components · derived state · indeterminate · tree data structures
checkbox-tree.why:
• Store checkedIds as a Set of ids. Each node derives its state from the set: all children in it means checked, none means unchecked, otherwise indeterminate. Set input.checked and input.indeterminate via a ref.
  • Toggling a parent means toggling every descendant id in the set. The ancestors' states then derive automatically on the next render.

cookie-consent.desc: A browser-round favourite at Atlassian: a pure UI flow with state kept in localStorage.
cookie-consent.q: How would you solve this problem? Cookie Consent Banner
cookie-consent.what:
Build a CookieConsent banner that appears at the bottom of the page after a delay. It has Accept All and Reject buttons, plus a Settings panel to toggle categories (Essential, Analytics, Marketing). Persist the choice in localStorage so returning users never see the banner again.

Requirements

  • The banner appears after a configurable delay (default 2s)
  • Accept All stores the choice and hides the banner
  • Reject stores the minimal choice and hides the banner
  • The Settings panel toggles categories; Save applies the selection
  • The Essential category is always on and disabled in the UI
  • The choice is persisted to localStorage; the banner is not shown again on reload
  • Fade/slide-in animation

Concepts: localStorage · setTimeout · conditional rendering · controlled toggles

context-menu.q: How would you solve this problem? Context Menu
context-menu.what:
Build a ContextMenu component. Right-clicking a target opens a custom menu at the cursor, with items that can have icons, a disabled state, and dividers. A left-click elsewhere, ESC, or scrolling closes it. The menu must clamp to the viewport so it never overflows off-screen. Nested submenus are a bonus.

Requirements

  • Right-click (onContextMenu) opens the menu at the cursor position
  • Viewport-aware: the position is clamped so the menu never goes off-screen
  • Closes on an outside left-click, ESC, scroll, and after an action
  • Items support a disabled state, icons, and dividers
  • Nested submenus open to the right of their parent
  • Right-clicking an item inside the open menu does not close the menu
  • The first item is focused when the menu opens

Concepts: onContextMenu · viewport clamping · window.innerWidth/Height · keyboard events
context-menu.why:
• Measure the menu after it renders, then clamp: left = min(x, innerWidth - rect.width - 8), top = min(y, innerHeight - rect.height - 8).
  • For dismissal, use a document mousedown listener that checks the menu ref, plus a scroll listener (capture: true) and a contextmenu listener for right-clicks elsewhere.

tic-tac-toe.q: How would you solve this problem? Tic-Tac-Toe Game
tic-tac-toe.what:
Build a TicTacToe game where two players alternate X and O. Highlight the winning line, detect draws, and show a turn indicator and a scoreboard. Add a game history with undo and time travel (jump to any past move), and a restart button.

Requirements

  • Clicking an empty cell places the current player's mark
  • Players alternate, with a clear turn indicator
  • Win detection across all 8 lines; the winning cells are highlighted
  • Draw detection when the board is full with no winner
  • Scoreboard: X wins, O wins, draws
  • A restart button resets the board
  • History with undo and time travel to any move
  • No moves are allowed after the game ends

Concepts: useState · winning combinations · derived state · immutable updates
tic-tac-toe.why:
• The board is an array of 9 cells. To check for a winner, loop over the predefined combinations of 3 indices and find one where all three cells are equal and non-empty.
  • History is an array of {board, player}. Time travel slices the history up to the target move index.

calculator.desc: A classic vanilla JS machine coding problem: digit entry, decimal handling, and chained operations.
calculator.q: How would you solve this problem? Calculator
calculator.what:
Build a Calculator with a display and buttons for digits, decimal point, +, -, x, /, %, +/-, Clear (C), and equals. Handle chained operations (5 + 3 = then + 2 =). Guard against divide-by-zero, leading decimals, multiple decimal points in one number, and leading zeros.

Requirements

  • All digits and the four basic operators work
  • Chained operations: 5 + 3 = 8, then + 2 = 10 (the result becomes the left operand)
  • Decimal input: only one dot per number; "5." is valid
  • Divide by zero shows Error and requires a clear
  • +/- toggles the sign; % divides the current value by 100
  • Clear (C) resets everything; the display shows the running value or expression
  • Keyboard support (digits, operators, Enter, Backspace) as a bonus

Concepts: state machine · operator precedence · string/number parsing · keyboard events
calculator.why:
• Track {display, left, operator, overwrite}. When a digit is pressed while overwrite is true, start a fresh number. When an operator is pressed and left already exists, compute left = op(left, current).
  • Apply % and +/- to the current display value before an operator or equals is pressed.

color-swatch.q: How would you solve this problem? Color Swatch Picker
color-swatch.what:
Build a ColorPicker with three sliders (R, G, B), each from 0 to 255. A large swatch shows the current color, and the hex and rgb() values update live. Support typing a validated hex value, a random-color button, and click-to-copy for the hex.

Requirements

  • Three range sliders (R/G/B) update the color live
  • The swatch background reflects the current RGB
  • The hex and rgb() outputs update as the sliders move
  • Hex input is validated (#RRGGBB); invalid input reverts
  • A random-color button sets all three sliders
  • Clicking the hex copies it to the clipboard (navigator.clipboard)
  • Number inputs beside the sliders stay in sync

Concepts: controlled range inputs · toString(16) · two-way sync · clipboard
color-swatch.why:
• Use a single source of truth: {r,g,b}. Both the sliders and the number inputs write to it. Hex = "#" + [r,g,b].map(v => v.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("").
  • For the hex input, match /^#?[0-9a-f]{6}$/i; if it is invalid, reset the input text to the current hex.

product-listing.q: How would you solve this problem? eCommerce Product Listing with Filters
product-listing.what:
Build a ProductListing page. A sidebar has category, price-range, and rating filters, and the main area renders product cards (image, title, price, rating, wishlist heart). Support sorting by price and rating, a result count, and an empty state. Wishlist toggles persist to localStorage and update a counter in the header.

Requirements

  • Category filter (single-select)
  • Price range slider + minimum rating filter (combined with AND)
  • Sort dropdown: price ascending/descending, rating descending
  • The result count reflects the filters; show an empty state when nothing matches
  • Product cards: image, title, price with strikethrough MRP, rating badge, wishlist heart
  • Toggling the wishlist updates a header counter and persists to localStorage
  • Filters apply instantly without a reload
  • Debounced price changes for smooth slider updates

Concepts: derived state · filter/sort pipelines · localStorage · debounce
product-listing.why:
• Keep the raw products[] plus a filter state {category, maxPrice, minRating, sort}. Derive the visible list with useMemo: apply the filters, then the sort.
  • Store the wishlist as a Set of ids in state and persist it on every change. The header count is set.size.

weather-app.q: How would you solve this problem? Weather App
weather-app.what:
Build a WeatherApp. The user can search by city (or use geolocation). Fetch data from the Open-Meteo API or any mock, and show the current temperature, condition, feels-like temperature, and a 5-day forecast. Add a Celsius/Fahrenheit toggle, persist the last city and unit, and handle loading, error, and empty states.

Requirements

  • City search input (debounced suggestions, or Enter to search)
  • Current conditions: temperature, condition, feels like, humidity, wind
  • 5-day forecast cards with an icon and high/low
  • A C / F unit toggle converts the displayed values
  • The last city and unit are persisted; a reload fetches automatically
  • Loading spinner, error banner with retry, and an empty state
  • Uses a key-free API (e.g. Open-Meteo) or a mock

Concepts: useEffect + async · fetch · state machines · unit conversion
weather-app.why:
• Model the UI state as {status: idle|loading|error|success, data}, separate from the shape of the data.
  • Convert with f = c * 9/5 + 32 at render time, and keep the metric values as the source of truth.

memory-game.q: How would you solve this problem? Memory Match Game
memory-game.what:
Build a MemoryGame with a grid of cards (4x4 by default, configurable). The player flips two cards: if they match, they stay face-up; otherwise they flip back after 800ms. Track moves and time, detect the win, and restart by reshuffling.

Requirements

  • A grid of paired cards, shuffled at the start
  • Clicking flips a card; at most two are face-up at a time
  • A match stays face-up; a mismatch flips back after a delay
  • Input is locked while two cards are being resolved
  • Move counter and elapsed timer
  • Win detection plus a completion banner
  • Restart reshuffles and resets
  • Configurable card count (4x4, 6x6)

Concepts: useState · setTimeout · Fisher-Yates shuffle · game state machine
memory-game.why:
• Cards are an array of {id, value, matched}. Keep flippedIds (max 2). After the second flip, compare the values; on a mismatch, use setTimeout with 800ms to flip them back.
  • Shuffle with Fisher-Yates: for i from n-1 down to 1, swap position i with a random index in [0..i].

poll-widget.q: How would you solve this problem? Poll / Vote Widget
poll-widget.what:
Build a Poll widget: a question with options and vote counts. Clicking an option highlights it as the user's choice, updates the counts, and shows percentage result bars. Persist the vote in localStorage so the same user cannot vote twice, and show live-updating totals.

Requirements

  • Render the options with their vote counts
  • Clicking an option registers the vote and updates the counts
  • Percentages are shown on result bars after voting
  • The vote is persisted to localStorage (one vote per user)
  • Results are hidden until the first vote (configurable reveal mode)
  • The total vote count is displayed
  • The voted option is highlighted distinctly

Concepts: useState · percentage math · localStorage · immutable updates
poll-widget.why:
• State: {question, options: [{id, text, votes}], votedId}. On a vote, map over the options to increment the chosen one and set votedId.
  • Percent = votes / total * 100. Set the result bar width to that percent and add a CSS transition on the fill.

expense-tracker.desc: CRUD + totals + filtering: the essential dashboard-style machine coding problem.
expense-tracker.q: How would you solve this problem? Expense Tracker
expense-tracker.what:
Build an ExpenseTracker. Users add expenses with a description, amount, category, and date, and see them in a list with edit and delete actions. Show the total spent, a per-category breakdown with progress bars, and a month filter. Persist everything to localStorage.

Requirements

  • Add-expense form (description, amount, category, date)
  • Validation: description required, amount greater than 0
  • Expense list sorted newest first, with edit and delete
  • Summary: total for the selected month, and budget vs spent
  • Category breakdown with bars and per-category totals
  • Month filter (all months or a specific month)
  • Expenses persisted to localStorage
  • Edit mode fills the form; saving updates the entry

Concepts: useReducer · localStorage · filtering/summarising · form validation
expense-tracker.why:
• State shape: [{id, desc, amount, category, date}]. Derive the totals and breakdowns with useMemo from the filtered list.
  • For editing, keep an editingId in state. The form initialises from that expense and dispatches UPDATE on save.

markdown-preview.desc: The classic editor-and-preview split: sanitise the HTML and avoid re-rendering on every keystroke.
markdown-preview.q: How would you solve this problem? Markdown Preview Editor
markdown-preview.what:
Build a MarkdownEditor. The left pane is a textarea and the right pane shows live-rendered HTML. Support headings, bold/italic, links, inline code, code blocks, lists, and blockquotes. Sanitise the output (no raw script tags), debounce the conversion, and show character and word counts.

Requirements

  • The live preview updates as you type (debounced by 200ms)
  • Supported syntax: # headings, **bold**, *italic*, [link](url), code, ``fences``, - lists, > quotes
  • Responsive two-column layout with editor-only / preview-only toggles
  • Sanitised HTML (strip script tags and onclick attributes)
  • Character and word counts in a status bar
  • Markdown persisted to localStorage

Concepts: controlled textarea · markdown parsing · sanitisation · debounce

seat-selector.q: How would you solve this problem? Movie Seat Selector
seat-selector.what:
Build a SeatSelector. Show a screen label at the top and a grid of seats in three states: available, taken, and selected. Clicking toggles selection (taken seats are disabled). Show a legend, the selected count, a price total, and an order summary, and enforce a maximum number of selectable seats.

Requirements

  • Grid generated from a rows x cols config
  • Three seat states: available / taken / selected
  • Taken seats (pre-seeded or passed as props) are not clickable
  • The selected count and running total update live
  • Configurable max selectable limit (default 8)
  • A legend showing the seat colors
  • A screen label at the top
  • The checkout button is enabled only when seats are selected

Concepts: 2D array state · Set for selection · derived totals · disable logic
seat-selector.why:
• Seats are a 2D array of {id, status}, and selected is a Set of seat ids. A click toggles the id and skips taken seats.
  • Total = selected.size * pricePerSeat. Show the summary only after the first selection.

playlist.desc: The Atlassian round: render a playlist, sort and filter it, and persist it.
playlist.q: How would you solve this problem? Music Playlist UI (Atlassian)
playlist.what:
Build a Playlist component from track data [{id, title, artist, duration, plays}]. Render the list with a header, sort by title/artist/plays/duration, filter by search, and show the total duration. Support playing a track (highlight it and show a mini player), removing a track, and reordering via up/down buttons or drag. Persist the playlist to localStorage.

Requirements

  • Render tracks with index, title, artist, duration, and plays
  • Sort dropdown: title, artist, plays, duration (ascending/descending)
  • A search box filters by title or artist
  • The total duration in the header updates with the filtered list
  • Clicking a track plays it (highlighted, and shown in the mini player)
  • Remove a track, and reorder with up/down buttons or drag
  • The playlist is persisted to localStorage
  • Empty state when no tracks match

Concepts: derived state · useMemo · sorting/filtering · localStorage
playlist.why:
• Derive the visible list from the raw tracks plus {sort, dir, query} with useMemo, and leave the raw data untouched.
  • To reorder, remove the item and insert it at the target index. Never mutate the array in place.

virtual-scroll.desc: Render 100,000 rows without a library: the classic performance challenge in machine coding rounds.
virtual-scroll.q: How would you solve this problem? Virtual Scroll List from Scratch

use-form.q: How would you solve this problem? useForm Hook (Formik-lite)

use-query.desc: The hardest custom hook challenge: caching, deduplication, and stale-while-revalidate.
use-query.q: How would you solve this problem? Build useQuery (mini React Query)

mini-router.q: How would you solve this problem? Build a Mini React Router
mini-router.what:
Build BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Link, useParams, and useNavigate. Support nested routes, dynamic segments (:id), and programmatic navigation.

Requirements

  • BrowserRouter: listen to popstate and provide the router context
  • Routes: find the best matching Route and render it
  • Route: match the path (support :param segments)
  • Link: renders , calls navigate on click, and does not trigger a full page reload
  • useParams: returns the current route params from the URL
  • useNavigate: returns a navigate(path) function that pushes to history
  • Nested routes: child Routes resolve relative to their parent

Concepts: Context · history API · pattern matching · useEffect · useRef

resizable-panels.q: How would you solve this problem? Resizable Split Panels
resizable-panels.why:
• On mousedown on the divider, attach mousemove and mouseup listeners to the document (not the divider). On mousemove, calculate the delta from the start position and clamp the new sizes within the min/max.
  • Use pointer events instead of mouse events to support touch. Call setPointerCapture on the divider in the pointerdown handler.

mini-state-mgmt.desc: Build Zustand from scratch: the ultimate React architecture challenge.
mini-state-mgmt.q: How would you solve this problem? Build a Mini State Management Library
mini-state-mgmt.what:
Build createStore(initialState), which returns a hook useStore(selector). Support atomic subscriptions (a component re-renders only when its selected slice changes), actions (store.setState), middleware, and a devtools-like getSnapshot.

Requirements

  • createStore(initialState) returns a useStore hook
  • useStore(selector): the component re-renders only when selector(state) changes
  • setState(partial | updater): merges a partial state or calls updater(prev)
  • Subscriptions: an internal pub-sub with listeners per component
  • Middleware support: intercept setState calls
  • getState() and subscribe(listener) on the store object

Concepts: useRef · useSyncExternalStore · pub-sub · shallow equality · closures
mini-state-mgmt.why:
• Use React 18's useSyncExternalStore(store.subscribe, () => selector(store.getState())). It handles concurrent rendering correctly.
  • If you roll your own subscription instead, compare the selected values with a shallow equality check and call forceUpdate only when shallowEqual(prevSelected, nextSelected) returns false.

undo-redo.q: How would you solve this problem? Undo / Redo with Command Pattern
undo-redo.what:
Build a reusable useHistory hook that implements undo/redo, and apply it to a simple drawing canvas or text editor. Each action is a Command with execute() and undo() methods.

Requirements

  • useHistory returns { state, execute(command), undo, redo, canUndo, canRedo }
  • Command interface: { execute, undo, description }
  • undo() reverts the last command
  • redo() reapplies a reverted command
  • The redo stack is cleared when a new command is executed
  • Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+Z (undo), Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z (redo)
  • Max history size (configurable, default 50)

Concepts: useReducer · command pattern · keyboard events · immutability

file-explorer.q: How would you solve this problem? File Explorer (Tree View)
file-explorer.what:
Build a FileExplorer that renders a nested folder/file tree. Clicking a folder expands or collapses it. Folders load their children lazily (async, on first expand) with loading and error states. Support icons, selection, keyboard navigation (arrows, Enter), and a breadcrumb for the selected path.

Requirements

  • Recursive rendering of folders and files
  • Expand/collapse folders with a chevron indicator
  • Lazy loading: children are fetched on first expand (mock API with a delay)
  • Loading spinner, and retry on fetch failure
  • Select a file or folder, highlight it, and show its path in a breadcrumb
  • Keyboard: Up/Down move the selection, Right expands, Left collapses, Enter opens
  • A side panel shows the selected file's size and type

Concepts: recursive components · async state · useCallback · keyboard events · tree data structures
file-explorer.why:
• Normalise the tree into a Map for O(1) lookups when selecting and expanding. Keep the expanded state as a Set of expanded ids.
  • For lazy loading: if node.children === undefined and node.isFolder, show a spinner, fetch, then set the children. Cache the results so re-expanding never refetches.

nested-comments.q: How would you solve this problem? Nested Comments (Reddit-style)
nested-comments.what:
Build a CommentSection with unlimited nesting. Each comment supports reply, edit, delete (which also removes its descendants), and like. Replies render recursively under their parent. Add a top-level input plus an inline reply box per comment. Every update must be immutable: never mutate the tree.

Requirements

  • The comment tree is rendered recursively to unlimited depth
  • Reply opens an inline input under that comment
  • Edit swaps the comment text for an inline textarea
  • Delete removes the comment and its descendants (with a confirm)
  • Like/dislike counter toggle
  • Collapse/expand hides and shows a comment's children
  • A top-level comment input
  • Persisted to localStorage
  • Sort toggle: newest first or most voted

Concepts: recursion · immutable tree updates · useReducer · reconciliation
nested-comments.why:
• A comment node looks like {id, author, text, votes, children, createdAt}. To update, walk the tree and rebuild each level, replacing only the node with the matching id, so every changed branch gets fresh references.
  • Helper: updateTree(comments, id, fn) returns a new array in which the matched node is replaced by fn(node) and every ancestor is rebuilt.

chat-app.q: How would you solve this problem? Chat App UI
chat-app.what:
Build a ChatApp: a contact list on the left and a conversation pane with messages (received on the left, sent on the right), a header, and a message input. Enter sends the message, and after a delay the other user auto-replies from a canned list. Show timestamps, bubbles with tails, a typing indicator, read ticks, and unread badges.

Requirements

  • The message list auto-scrolls to the bottom on a new message
  • Bubbles: sent on the right (blue), received on the left (grey), with timestamps
  • A typing indicator while the simulated reply is pending
  • Auto-reply from canned responses after 1-2s
  • Left pane: contacts with a last-message preview and an unread badge
  • Read receipt: double ticks turn blue when read
  • Enter sends; the send action is disabled while the input is empty
  • Chat persisted to localStorage

Concepts: useRef for auto-scroll · useEffect · timers · derived previews
chat-app.why:
• Auto-scroll: call scrollRef.current.scrollIntoView() in a useEffect keyed on messages.length, but only when the user is already near the bottom.
  • Typing indicator: keep a pendingReply state. Show a typing bubble while it is true, then replace it with the reply message.

minesweeper.q: How would you solve this problem? Minesweeper
minesweeper.what:
Build a Minesweeper game. Generate an N x M board with a configurable mine count. A left-click reveals a cell, and clicking a mine ends the game. Revealing a cell with zero adjacent mines flood-fills the empty region. A right-click places a flag. Show a remaining-mine counter and a timer, and win when every safe cell is revealed. Difficulty presets: Beginner 9x9/10, Intermediate 16x16/40, Expert 30x16/99.

Requirements

  • Board generation with configurable size and mine count
  • The first click is never a mine (defer mine placement or regenerate)
  • Adjacent-mine numbers are shown on reveal
  • Flood-fill reveal for cells with zero adjacent mines (BFS/DFS)
  • Right-click places a flag; flags count against the remaining mines
  • The timer starts on the first reveal
  • Win: all safe cells revealed. Loss: clicking a mine reveals all mines
  • Restart and difficulty presets

Concepts: 2D arrays · flood fill (BFS/DFS) · randomness · game state machine

snake.desc: The classic arcade game on a grid: game loop, collision, and score.
snake.q: How would you solve this problem? Snake Game
snake.what:
Build a Snake game on a grid. Arrow keys (or WASD) change the direction, and the snake moves on a fixed interval that speeds up as it eats food. Eating grows the snake and increases the score. Hitting a wall or itself ends the game with an overlay and a restart option. Show the score and the high score (localStorage).

Requirements

  • The snake moves continuously on a grid (interval-based game loop)
  • Arrow/WASD controls with a direction lock (no reversing into itself)
  • Food spawns at a random free cell; eating it grows the snake
  • Speed increases with the score (the interval shortens)
  • Wall or self collision means game over, with an overlay
  • The score and the persisted high score are displayed
  • Pause/resume (Space) and restart
  • Rendered with divs or canvas

Concepts: game loop · queue (snake body) · collision detection · useRef for state
snake.why:
• The snake is an array of {x,y} cells, head first. To move, unshift the new head and pop the tail unless the snake just ate. Keep the snake and direction in refs so the interval closure always reads fresh values.
  • Direction lock: reject a turn when (dx + nx) === 0 and (dy + ny) === 0.

date-picker.q: How would you solve this problem? Calendar / Date Range Picker
date-picker.what:
Build a DateRangePicker: a month grid with prev/next navigation. The first click sets the range start and the second completes it, with in-range dates highlighted. Clicking when a range already exists starts a new one. Support presets, min/max constraints, keyboard navigation, and onChange({start, end}).

Requirements

  • Month grid: weekday headers, correct day alignment, today highlighted
  • Prev/Next month navigation plus a jump-to-today button
  • Range selection: first click sets the start, second sets the end; hovering previews the range
  • Clicking when a range exists starts a new range
  • Presets: Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, This month, Last 30 days
  • Dates outside min/max are disabled
  • Keyboard: arrows move focus, Enter selects, Escape cancels
  • onChange({start, end}) with start <= end

Concepts: Date object · date arithmetic · range logic · grid generation

auth-flow.desc: Flipkart asks for the full flow: login, session, protected routing, and profile.
auth-flow.q: How would you solve this problem? Login / Profile Flow with Protected Routes
auth-flow.what:
Build an AuthFlow demo: a login form with mock validation, a session Context, and protected routes. Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login (and sent back to the requested page after logging in). A profile page shows the user and a logout button. Simulate a fake API with delays and error paths, and persist the session token in localStorage.

Requirements

  • Login form: email + password with validation and error messages
  • Fake auth API (a Promise with a delay) with success and failure paths
  • Session kept in Context and persisted to localStorage
  • ProtectedRoute redirects unauthenticated users to /login
  • After login, redirect back to the originally requested route
  • The profile page shows user info; logout clears the session
  • A signup tab validates the password confirmation
  • Loading state on the submit button

Concepts: Context · protected routing · localStorage · redirect logic · form validation

error-boundary.desc: Resilience in React: class-based boundaries and the modern hook for async errors.
error-boundary.q: How would you solve this problem? Error Boundary
error-boundary.what:
Build an ErrorBoundary class component with a fallback UI, a reset, and error reporting. Handle render errors and, via a useErrorHandler hook, async errors thrown in effects or callbacks.

Requirements

  • A class component using getDerivedStateFromError and componentDidCatch
  • Renders a fallback UI (custom or default) instead of crashing the app
  • A reset button clears the error and retries rendering the children
  • Reports the error + errorInfo to an onError callback
  • useErrorHandler(err) throws during render so async errors reach the boundary
  • Multiple boundaries wrap different regions of the app
  • The boundary is keyed so its state resets cleanly

Concepts: class components · getDerivedStateFromError · componentDidCatch · error reporting
error-boundary.why:
• class ErrorBoundary extends Component { static getDerivedStateFromError(error) { return {error}; } componentDidCatch(error, info) { onError?.(error, info); } }
  • useErrorHandler keeps a ref to a setState call and returns (err) => { if (err) throwRef.current(err); }. The error is rethrown during render inside the boundary's subtree, which triggers the boundary.

custom-hooks.q: How would you solve this problem? Custom Hooks Library
custom-hooks.what:
Build a library of reusable hooks: useDebouncedValue, useLocalStorage, useClickOutside, useWindowSize, usePrevious, and useIntersection. Each must clean up after itself, return stable references, and be generic. Write a small demo page that exercises every hook.

Requirements

  • useDebouncedValue(value, delay): returns the value once it has not changed for the given delay
  • useLocalStorage(key, initial): reads on mount, writes on change, and syncs across tabs
  • useClickOutside(ref, handler): a mousedown outside the ref triggers the handler; the listener is removed on unmount
  • useWindowSize(): returns {width, height}, with debounced updates
  • usePrevious(value): returns the value from the previous render
  • useIntersection(ref, options): returns {isIntersecting, entry} via IntersectionObserver
  • All hooks return stable references (no new functions on every render)

Concepts: custom hooks · useCallback/useMemo · useEffect cleanup · generics
custom-hooks.why:
• useDebouncedValue: a useEffect that starts a setTimeout(delay) to update state, with clearTimeout in the cleanup so every value change restarts the timer.
  • useLocalStorage: useState initialised from the key, a useEffect that writes on change, and a window "storage" listener to sync other tabs.
